queue.name: Opening Break
queue.expectation: OOS 0.00 to +0.05R net at 1 tick per side. The lab's own SPX table put OOS at +0.018R (0.25 tick) and -0.032R (0.5 tick); NQ's wider point range may carry it. Honest odds of a pass: about 1 in 3.
queue.plain_words: The one signal that survived the 1,492: a break away from the session open by 0.45 of the 14-day range, confirmed by a 5-minute close on the right side of the day's VWAP, taken once per day before 11:00 ET, stop 0.25 of the range, target 0.60, flat by 15:50. Re-run on Nasdaq and S&P futures at micro-contract cost.
lesson: The edge is real (+0.120R over 929 trades) but jagged: the worst stretch is 15R deep. The largest size that keeps a funded account alive is 0.15% risk per trade, and at that size it earns about 2.7% a year.
The lever is the drawdown, not the entry: a filter that removes the losing stretch (or the losing market) is the one declared fix worth trying.

queue.name: Patient Break
queue.expectation: Fewer trades (maybe a third), higher expectancy per trade; may fall under 200 OOS trades and land INSUFFICIENT.
queue.plain_words: The Opening Break taken only on days the daily trend agrees (above the 150-day line for longs, below for shorts) and only when the first 30 minutes already moved at least a quarter of the 14-day range. Jae's 'know when the market will move', as a rule.
lesson: The edge is real (+0.133R over 431 trades) but jagged: the worst stretch is 18R deep. The largest size that keeps a funded account alive is 0.14% risk per trade, and at that size it earns about 1.3% a year.
The lever is the drawdown, not the entry: a filter that removes the losing stretch (or the losing market) is the one declared fix worth trying.

queue.name: Swing Pullback
queue.expectation: Small positive, low drawdown: about +0.05R, 40-60 trades a year across three markets. A seat only if uncorrelated to the trend book and return/drawdown > 1. Honest odds: 1 in 4.
queue.plain_words: When a market is above its 150-day line and closes at a 3-day low, buy at the next close. Sell at the next close after it prints a 5-day high, after seven days, or if it closes 1.5 twenty-day ranges below the entry (the stop). Nasdaq (QQQ), gold (GLD) and Bitcoin, on the money desk's own daily closes.
lesson: The edge is real (+0.151R over 608 trades) but jagged: the worst stretch is 39R deep. The largest size that keeps a funded account alive is 0.20% risk per trade, and at that size it earns about 3.2% a year.
The lever is the drawdown, not the entry: a filter that removes the losing stretch (or the losing market) is the one declared fix worth trying.
By market: works on GLD, QQQ, loses on BTC.

queue.name: Gold After the News
queue.blocker: no news calendar yet (calendar_pull.py on the server)
queue.expectation: Real but rare (about 30 trades a year): cannot reach 200 out-of-sample trades before ~2030 on 2022→ data — most likely INSUFFICIENT; may only qualify as a sizing overlay.
queue.plain_words: On CPI, FOMC and payroll days, trade gold in the direction of the first 30 minutes after the release, stop at the other side of that 30-minute move, out after two more sessions. Micro gold futures cost.

queue.name: Gold Ride-the-Run
queue.expectation: More return per unit held, but the cap means less held on average; return/drawdown probably does not improve. The uncapped variant (adds above the vol target) is expected to add return and a deeper hole — leverage. Honest odds: 1 in 5.
queue.plain_words: Hold gold at half its normal size; add a quarter each time gold prints a new 20-day high, up to the normal size (the vol-target cap); a 20-day low ends the run and resets to half. Compared with simply holding gold at full size.
lesson: Gold Ride-the-Run vs the live book out of sample: Sharpe -0.07, CAGR -4.5 pts, max drawdown +5.7 pts (positive = shallower).
Shallower hole, weaker return — it is a risk dial, not an edge; the vol target already does this job.
Average size held: overlay 0.76 of the vol target vs 1.00 — it holds less, so lower return is arithmetic, not a finding.

queue.name: Momentum Check
queue.expectation: Dead after 2022 (independent rechecks put the slope near zero). Expected FAIL; it is on the list so the question is closed with a number.
queue.plain_words: If the first half-hour of the Nasdaq session went up, buy at 15:30 and sell at the close; if it went down, the reverse. The academic intraday-momentum effect (Gao, Han, Li, Zhou 2018), one honest test at micro-contract cost.
lesson: No signal out of sample: gross expectancy -0.011R before any cost over 1395 trades. This is the rule, not the venue.
The only honest fix is a filter (one declared condition that removes the losing trades) — or close the family.

queue.name: Volume Break
queue.expectation: Modest help, inside noise: a few hundredths of an R, not a verdict-changer.
queue.plain_words: The Opening Break taken only when the first 30 minutes traded at least 1.2 times the usual volume for that half hour.
lesson: It works on ES and not on NQ — a market fix (drop the losers) is the declared next step.

queue.name: Two-Speed Trend
queue.expectation: Fails on turnover — the 20-day line flips far more often than the 150-day; Sharpe about the same, costs higher. Expected FAIL.
queue.plain_words: The live book with its 150-day line replaced by two lines: a 20-day and a 250-day. Half a position when one says up, full when both do, none when neither. Gold stays always held. Same weights, vol targets, costs and rails as the money desk.
lesson: Two-Speed Trend vs the live book out of sample: Sharpe -0.20, CAGR -3.5 pts, max drawdown -3.2 pts (positive = shallower).
Worse on both quality and hole — the change removes nothing and adds nothing. Closed unless a declared fix names a mechanism.
Turnover out of sample: 13.3x a year vs the book's 6.5x.

queue.name: Swing Pullback — fix 1 (trailing-edge market filter)
queue.expectation: Bitcoin drops out once its losing stretch is visible; expectancy per trade rises; but the 2021 hole came from all three markets at once, so the worst stretch probably stays deep and the return at the surviving size stays under 10%/yr. Likely still FAIL. This is fix 1 of 3 for the family.
queue.plain_words: The Swing Pullback, but a market is only traded while its own last three years of these trades (the ones already closed) show a profit. No market is dropped by hand — the rule drops it, in time, with no look-ahead. Answers the first test's lesson: Bitcoin lost, gold and Nasdaq worked.
lesson: The edge is real (+0.149R over 513 trades) but jagged: the worst stretch is 43R deep. The largest size that keeps a funded account alive is 0.20% risk per trade, and at that size it earns about 2.7% a year.
The lever is the drawdown, not the entry: a filter that removes the losing stretch (or the losing market) is the one declared fix worth trying.
By market: works on GLD, QQQ, loses on BTC.

queue.name: Opening Break — fix 1 (range form)
queue.expectation: Cost per trade falls to about 0.01–0.02R. The signal itself is untested here (the literature's ORB results are modest and unreplicated with slippage). Worst stretch probably still deeper than 10R. Honest odds: 1 in 4. If it fails on the signal (gross ≤ +0.05R), the family's cost lever is closed and only a market fix remains.
queue.plain_words: The first 30 minutes set a range. After 10:00, a 5-minute close above the range buys, below it sells; the stop is the other side of the range; one attempt per day, no entries after 12:00, flat by 15:55. The stop is 5–10 times wider than the proven form's, so each tick of cost is a much smaller slice of R — the cost lever, declared as fix 1 of the opening-breakout family.
lesson: The signal is there (+0.062R gross, 2610 trades) and costs eat it (0.025R per trade → +0.037R net).
The lever is cost/venue: a cheaper contract, fewer ticks of slippage, or a wider stop that makes each tick smaller in R.
